land.text: the Peshawar valley (Gandara satrapy, from c. 535 BCE) and the Taksasila country to the Jhelum (Hindush, c. 518 BCE)

successors.note: Cyrus took 'Gandhara proper' c. 535 BCE and Darius's army 'pushed to the Jhelum River' c. 518 BCE. The pages do not say who held the Kashmir valley after 518; it is left to nobody.

capitals.name: Takshashila (Taxila)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Taksasila Puskalavati'; Mahajanapadas page 'Its later capital was Taksashila', the earlier being Pushkalavati (Charsadda, 34.15N 71.74E), which fell to Cyrus c. 535 BCE. No page dates the move. Coordinates are Taxila's.

correction.text: Gandhara 'on both sides of the Indus River', 'the modern Rawalpindi District' and 'Peshawar District', with its cities Taksasila and Puskalavati and 'the valley of Kasmira', part of the kingdom by the 6th century BCE

keyframe_review.note: Mislocated: the 4,988 km2 shape (centroid 74.37E 33.39N) lies in the Pir Panjal around Rajouri, 150 km east of Taxila and 250 km from Peshawar; that is where the Mahajanapadas page puts Kamboja's capital Rajapura ('modern Rajori'), while Cliopatria's Kamboja shape (73.3E 33.5N) sits on the Rawalpindi plateau next to Taxila: the two rows look swapped. The corrected shape is the Peshawar valley (gazetteer 'Gandhara', about 49,000 km2), Taxila and the Kashmir valley, about 63,000 km2 (the gazetteer's Gandhara already contains Taxila's 60 km); the infobox gives no area. It holds -600..-536.

correction.text: the Taksasila country east of the Indus and the Kashmir valley, left to the kingdom after Cyrus's annexation of 'Gandhara proper'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Around 535 BCE' Cyrus 'annexed a large region to the west of the Indus River', and 'the annexation under Cyrus was limited to Gandhara proper' (kingdom page); the kingdom keeps the Taksasila country east of the Indus and Kashmir until Darius's army 'pushed to the Jhelum River' around 518 BCE.

correction.text: the eastern remnant of keyframe janapada-of-gandhara_-535, for -535..-519 only; the Rajouri shape as drawn belongs to no state of these years and after -518 the land is Achaemenid

keyframe_review.note: Mislocated as the -600 shape and wrongly dated: the Peshawar valley was Achaemenid from c. 535 BCE and the whole kingdom from c. 518 BCE ('secure occupation of Gandhara' in 518; the Behistun inscription, c. 518 BCE, lists Gandara); the kingdom infobox's 'Conquered by the Achaemenid Empire: c. 500 BCE' is an approximation of the same event. Cliopatria keeps the row to -501.

region.text: Gandhara 'on both sides of the Indus River', 'the modern Rawalpindi District' and 'Peshawar District', with its cities Taksasila and Puskalavati and 'the valley of Kasmira', part of the kingdom by the 6th century BCE

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: Gandhara, ruled from Taksasila and Puskalavati, holds the Peshawar valley, the Indus crossing and Kashmir. 'By the 6th century BCE, Gandhara had expanded to include the valley of Kasmira'; rulers 'c. 700 BCE: Nagnajit', 'c. 550 BCE: Pukkusati'; the Madrakas, Kekayas, Usinaras and Shivis were 'under Gandhari suzerainty' (late Vedic, undated, not drawn). -600 is the Mahajanapada convention; the infobox's 'Established c. 2000 BCE' is not drawn.

region.text: 'Gandhara proper': 'a large region to the west of the Indus River', 'the entire Peshawar Valley' with Puskalavati

ledger.note: c. 535 BCE: Cyrus the Great annexes Gandhara west of the Indus. 'Around 535 BCE' the Persian army 'annexed a large region to the west of the Indus River'; 'Cyrus probably went as far as the banks of the Indus river' and organised it as the Gandhara satrapy, 'the entire Peshawar Valley' bounded by Swat, Afghanistan, the Indus and Kohat, capital Pushkalavati. Kingdom page: 'The annexation under Cyrus was limited to Gandhara proper'. The Mahajanapadas page gives only Cyrus's reign (558-530 BCE) 'or the first year of Darius'.

region.text: the Taksasila country east of the Indus and the Kashmir valley, left to the kingdom after Cyrus's annexation of 'Gandhara proper'

ledger.note: c. 518 BCE: Darius I's army reaches the Jhelum; Taksasila falls and Gandhara ends as a kingdom. 'Around 518 BCE' the army pushed 'to the Jhelum River', 'secure occupation of Gandhara' is dated to this year, and the Behistun inscription (c. 518 BCE) lists Gandara; the Hindush satrapy, 'the Greater Punjab region' bounded by Hazara, the Indus and the Jhelum, had its capital at 'Bhir Mound in Taxila'. Kingdom page: it is unknown whether Pukkusati 'remained in power after the Achaemenid conquest as a Persian vassal' or was 'replaced by a Persian satrap'; infobox 'Conquered by the Achaemenid Empire: c. 500 BCE'. The pages do not say who held the Kashmir valley after 518; it goes to nobody. Cliopatria ends the row in -501.

wars.name: Achaemenid conquest of the Indus Valley

zones.text: the Taksasila country to the Jhelum

wars.outcome: 'Persian victory'; 'Annexation of the Indus Valley by the Persians': the Gandhara satrapy under Cyrus (c. 535 BCE), Hindush and the Jhelum frontier under Darius I (c. 518 BCE). Gandara is last listed as a province on the tomb of Artaxerxes II, c. 358 BCE.
wars.note: Infobox 'c. 535/518 BCE - 323 BCE'; the campaign 'paused after Cyrus's death around 530 BCE'. Belligerents as the infobox lists them; the Kamboja and Sindhu-Sauvira sides belong to other dossiers.

wars.name: Pukkusati's war with Pradyota of Avanti
wars.outcome: 'Pukkusati was successful in this struggle with Pradyota'; no land changed hands.
wars.note: Undated; Pukkusati c. 550 BCE. The Avanti page: 'Pradyota waged war on Pushkarasarin, king of Takshashila'.

wars.name: Pukkusati's war with the Pandavas
wars.outcome: 'war broke out between him and the Pandava tribe'; outcome and land not given.
wars.note: Undated; the page adds that Pukkusati 'also engaged in friendly relations with the king Bimbisara of Magadha'.

certainty.note: The Indus is the only line the pages give (Cyrus's annexation 'to the west of the Indus River'); the Kashmir and Swat edges are the gazetteer's regions.

sources.title: Gandhāra (kingdom)
sources.note: Identity, infobox (c. 2000 BCE to c. 500 BCE, Taksasila and Puskalavati), Rawalpindi and Peshawar, Kashmir in the 6th century, Nagnajit and Pukkusati, Pradyota and the Pandavas, Cyrus's annexation 'limited to Gandhara proper', Behistun.

sources.title: Achaemenid conquest of the Indus Valley
sources.note: Cyrus c. 535 BCE west of the Indus, Darius c. 518 BCE to the Jhelum, the Gandhara and Hindush satrapies and their bounds, Behistun c. 518, the tribute, the end c. 358-323 BCE.

sources.title: Mahajanapadas
sources.note: Overview of the sixteen states ('from the sixth to fourth centuries BCE'), the Mahajanapada convention behind every -600 start, and the per-state location notes; shared by the five janapada dossiers of batch sa-01-a.

notes: Cliopatria's two identical Gandhara shapes are at Rajouri in the Pir Panjal, where the Mahajanapadas page puts Kamboja's capital Rajapura, while its Kamboja shapes sit on the Rawalpindi plateau beside Taxila: the two rows appear swapped, and the Kamboja agent (sa-01) should check its shapes against this note. Both Gandhara shapes are marked wrong and replaced by the Peshawar valley, Taxila and the Kashmir valley (about 63,000 km2 against 4,988). The end is moved from Cliopatria's -501 to -518 (Darius's push to the Jhelum and the Behistun listing), with a new keyframe for the eastern remnant -535..-519 after Cyrus took the Peshawar valley; the Achaemenid dossier should carry the matching gains in -535 and -518 (the Achaemenid Empire row -550..-327 belongs to another group). Unsettled: whether Pukkusati stayed on as a Persian vassal; who held Kashmir after 518 (left to nobody); the Gandhari suzerainty over the Madrakas, Kekayas, Usinaras and Shivis (undated, not drawn); the Mulaka-like Sindhu-Sauvira belligerent has no row. Gazetteer: Gandhara, Kashmir Valley and Taxila are present; Charsadda/Pushkalavati (34.15N 71.74E) is not (used only in a capital note).
